architectural_units.name: Frontend
architectural_units.description: The client, which we also call frontEnd, is responsible for the presentation and user experience of the application, encapsulating the interface logic and the coordination of calls to the server API.

architectural_units.name: Backend
architectural_units.description: For the server, the backEnd, Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern.

architectural_units.name: Leader
architectural_units.description: This microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

architectural_units.name: Portal
architectural_units.description: The portal microservice has as its main function to offer a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications.

architectural_units.name: Access Control
architectural_units.description: The Access Control microservice has as its main objective the management of user authentication and their permissions within the application.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log
architectural_units.description: The Communication Log microservice has as its main purpose to record all communications that occur within the system, both between microservices and with external services.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler
architectural_units.description: It has as its main function the planning and programming of processes within the system.

architectural_units.name: View
architectural_units.description: The component we call View is formed by the HTML and SCSS files of each component that make up the application.

architectural_units.name: ViewModel
architectural_units.description: The ViewModel component groups the TS files of the components and the services they have associated.

architectural_units.name: Model
architectural_units.description: Models are the TypeScript classes that define the data contract consumed by the view and the ViewModel.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer (Controllers)
architectural_units.description: The presentation layer receives requests and builds responses.

architectural_units.name: Business Logic Layer (Services)
architectural_units.description: The services offer the interface and implementation of all the business logic of the application.

architectural_units.name: Domain Layer (Models)
architectural_units.description: The models represent the internal and persistent structure of the system entities reflecting identically the stored information.

architectural_units.name: Contract Layer (DTO/Mappers)
architectural_units.description: Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) act as information containers that allow structuring the data necessary for each request.

architectural_units.name: Data Access Layer (Repositories)
architectural_units.description: Repositories are responsible for performing queries on the database.

architectural_units.name: Angular
architectural_units.description: Angular is a web development framework created by Google, based on the programming language superset of JavaScript called TypeScript.

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Spring Boot is a framework that simplifies the creation of Java applications based on Spring.

architectural_units.name: HTTP
architectural_units.description: The message exchange protocol used in this case is HTTP.

architectural_units.name: JSON
architectural_units.description: The data format used is JSON.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services
architectural_units.description: The provider for this project is Amazon Web Services which has a wide catalog of cloud services and resources.

architectural_units.name: REST
architectural_units.description: Spring Boot, which provides a platform for exposing a REST API.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The application has an architecture based on microservices.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application also applies a cloud architecture.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application follows the Client-Server pattern which organizes the code into two differentiated components: the client and the server.

patterns.name: MVVM
patterns.description: Angular applies the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern, since its architecture is based on components and services.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern with which responsibilities are separated.
